name_reason: Compliant: data_fd2_ prefix for a game global, battle_ core-table domain, descriptor reflects both the data shape (counter array) and the meaningful slot count (5slot = 5 sprite slots, matching the byte[5] layout, a domain dimension not a Ghidra address residue). No address residue in the name.
purpose: Per-slot transient blit counter (5 slots) for the variant-C 5-slot radial summon animation; runtime scratch.
logic_summary: Zero-init BSS. The sole user fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_c_5slot_radial clears all 5 entries to 0 in the state-3 setup loop, seeds a slot to 5 in the state 4/5 loop when the scratch sprite-id (angle_accumulator) is 1, then in the state-5 post-loop advance: for each nonzero entry, blits it as the sprite-id (trailing-streak effect), increments it, and wraps it back to 0 when it reaches 10. Accessed only as byte[5] indexed 0..4 (stride 1).
element_semantics: Each element is an unsigned 8-bit transient blit counter for one of the 5 sprite slots: 0 = inactive, else a running 1..9 value reused as the blit sprite-id and wrapped 10->0.
notes: datatype byte[5] confirmed by xref boundaries: 0x54091 belongs to this array (slot 1), 0x54095 is the separate angle_accumulator symbol, so the array is exactly slots 0..4. is_const=false: many game WRITE xrefs (0x26ecf/0x26f67/0x271b7/0x27120/...) and all-zero on-disk image (BSS). Source comment block (anisummn.c lines 1410-1419) already accurate and concise -> kept verbatim. Function plate of fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_c_5slot_radial already documents [0x54090] consistently; no separate data-address plate exists and none needed (not a contradiction), so plate left untouched. No logic/equivalence issues.
